methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cemvita is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Moji and Tara Karimi that has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (Linamar, LNZA) and 8 private firms including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, and Redwood Materials, all operating in the same sector and stage window.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $30M raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $57M. Peer-median valuation examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median of this set is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $48M (low, conservative stage-progression floor), $528M (median), and $1.1B (high, peer-median ceiling). The median estimate of $528M reflects the substantial gap between early-stage capital deployed and peer valuations at adjacent stages. Key uncertainties include technology maturity relative to comparables, capital efficiency, and whether Cemvita's competitive position within climate-tech justifies positioning toward the peer median or closer to stage-based expectations. Further diligence on unit economics and go-to-market traction would narrow this range.
